title: IB SEHS Revision Plan: Your Final Three Weeks
summary: IB SEHS revision plan for November: organize topic triage, question practice, timed papers, recovery, and your final three weeks with confidence.
body_markdown:
Three weeks is enough time to make meaningful progress in IB Sports, Exercise and Health Science if you revise selectively. An effective **IB SEHS revision plan** for November should move through three stages: diagnose weaknesses, repair the concepts costing you marks, and rehearse complete papers under timed conditions.


The challenge is deciding what deserves your attention when SEHS is one of several subjects on your timetable. This plan uses focused 45-60 minute blocks, protects rest, and leaves room for other exams.


### Your three-week revision checklist


Before your November exams, aim to:


- Audit the syllabus and classify topics as red, amber or green
- Repair weak concepts using retrieval and targeted questions
- Practise multiple-choice, data-based, short-answer and extended-response formats
- Complete and review at least two timed paper simulations
- Record why errors happened and retest those weaknesses
- Protect sleep and reduce study volume during the final day


The current SEHS course covers exercise physiology and nutrition, biomechanics, and sports psychology and motor learning. Paper 1 includes multiple-choice questions and data-based and experimental work; Paper 2 combines short-answer and extended-response questions. Confirm the syllabus, format and duration applicable to your examination session with your school.


Use the[complete IB SEHS HL and SL guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ultimate-guide-to-ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-hl-and-sl) to orient yourself before planning individual sessions.


### Week one: diagnose before you revise


Opening the first chapter feels organized, but it gives familiar and unfamiliar material equal attention. Start by finding out what you can actually retrieve and apply.


### Days 1-2: map your weaknesses


Sample questions across the syllabus using the[IB SEHS Questionbank and resource hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-sports-exercise-and-health-science-sehs-new-syllabus) . Label each topic:


- **Red:** you cannot explain it without support
- **Amber:** you understand it but struggle with application
- **Green:** you can answer unfamiliar questions accurately


Recognition is not mastery. If a diagram looks familiar but you cannot explain its logic with your notes closed, classify it as amber or red.


Keep an error log with four columns: topic, mistake, cause and next action. Distinguish missing knowledge from misreading data, overlooking command terms or running out of time. Each cause needs a different repair.


### Days 3-6: repair priority topics


As a flexible starting point, give 60% of SEHS time to red topics, 30% to amber and 10% to green. Adjust according to your diagnostic results.


Use the[guide to IB SEHS self-study resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/best-ib-sehs-resources-self-study) to choose focused support. Read the relevant Study Notes, close them, and explain the concept from memory. Flashcards can test definitions and processes; AI Chat can help clarify a relationship you cannot explain. Check explanations against your course materials, then attempt Questionbank problems independently.


These[IB SEHS revision strategies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revision-strategies-that-work-for-ib-sports-science-exams) offer further guidance on retrieval and spacing.


### Day 7: consolidate


Complete a mixed 45-minute set, review your errors and update your topic ratings. Keep the afternoon lighter so you begin week two with enough concentration for demanding practice.


A student asks whether sleep counts as preparation while a tiny coach praises the training strategy.


### Week two: turn knowledge into marks


Understanding a concept and communicating it under assessment conditions are separate skills. This week connects them through deliberate practice and correction.


### Rotate question formats


Alternate multiple-choice sets, data interpretation, experimental questions, short answers and extended responses. Practise identifying variables, interpreting trends, evaluating methods and explaining scientific relationships.


A useful 50-minute session contains 25 minutes of closed-book questions, 15 minutes of marking and 10 minutes of correction. Rewrite the part that failed, then explain why your revised answer meets the question. This makes correction an active decision rather than a copying exercise.


### Read command terms carefully


Underline the command term before answering. Identify requires a different response from explain, compare or evaluate. Translate the instruction into an action before you write.


For extended responses, outline the main ideas briefly. Connect each scientific claim to its consequence in an exercise, sporting or health context. The guide to[learning IB SEHS through case studies](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/using-case-studies-for-better-learning-in-ib-sports-science) can help you select relevant examples.


Keep other subjects visible. On an SEHS priority day, schedule one or two substantial blocks. When another exam takes priority, maintain contact with 15-20 minutes of Flashcards or error-log recall.


### Week three: rehearse the complete task


Timed practice reveals what changes under pressure. Use Exam mode for uninterrupted attempts, keeping Study Notes and AI Chat closed until you finish.


### Days 15-17: simulate and diagnose


Sit a complete paper using the duration and conditions specified for your level and session. Put your phone away and continue after difficult questions rather than stopping to investigate them.


Mark your attempt, using RevisionDojo’s Grading tools where appropriate. Look for patterns: incomplete explanations, missed command terms, calculations taking too long, or omitted units. Spend the next session repairing the two most costly patterns.


### Days 18-19: test your adjustments


Complete another timed paper and apply one specific improvement from your first attempt. You might plan extended answers, move on sooner or reserve checking time.


Predicted Papers and Mock Exams can provide additional rehearsal material. Use Tutors for persistent conceptual difficulties. The Coursework Library can support coursework understanding, while your final exam sessions should stay focused on the assessed questions.


### Days 20-21: reduce the load


Shorten sessions during the final 48 hours. Review your error log, retrieve essential concepts and complete brief mixed questions. Avoid opening a large new resource without a specific purpose.


Prepare your materials, confirm your school’s exam instructions and stop at a sensible hour.


### Make the next action clear


Start with a mixed diagnostic, then let your errors determine tomorrow’s work. RevisionDojo connects practice, explanations and feedback so each session has a clear purpose. Three weeks become more useful when every attempt tells you what to do next.
